evidence: Verg. A. 5.231: possunt, quia posse videntur
terms.comment: The plain “because”, and the answer to “why?” (Quārē? — Quia …).

terms.grammar: conjunction: with the indicative for the speaker’s own reason, with the subjunctive for a reason reported or rejected
evidence: Varr. LL 5.76: noctua, quod noctū canit et vigilat
Hor. S. 1.6.119–120: nōn sollicitus, mihi quod crās surgendum sit māne
terms.comment: As common as quia; the mood shows whose reason it is. A reason denied: nōn quod … sed quia, not because … but because. Stressed, proptereā quod, “for the reason that”.

evidence: Varr. RR 3.6.1: līberē licet dīcās, quoniam discessit Fircellius
terms.comment: A reason both speakers know: see since (because).

phrases.english: they can, because they think they can

phrases.latin: nēmō enim patriam quia magna est amat, sed quia sua
phrases.english: no one loves his country because it is great, but because it is his

phrases.latin: noctua, quod noctū canit et vigilat
phrases.english: the little owl (is so called) because it sings and stays awake at night

phrases.latin: deinde eō dormītum, nōn sollicitus, mihi quod crās surgendum sit māne
phrases.english: then I go to bed, not worried that I must get up early tomorrow
